## Ahu Te Pito Kura: an optional excursion to Easter Island's moai

[Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/) is an archaeological site on Rapa Nui where you can see a large fallen moai. Unlike some of the restored statues at [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), this figure lies on the ground. The stop reveals how differently the island's monuments have survived and why comparing several ceremonial sites on one excursion is so rewarding.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with an optional visit to Te Pito Kura. The main [14-day itinerary through Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) covers mainland South America: Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca, Uyuni, the Atacama Desert, and Santiago. **Easter Island and Te Pito Kura belong to a separate 3-day, 2-night extension.** They are not compulsory stops during the main 14 days.

## What the island extension includes

The optional itinerary takes in several important Rapa Nui sites: [Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/), [the Rano Raraku quarry](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), Ahu Tongariki, Te Pito Kura, and [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). Each stop illustrates a different chapter of the island's history. Statues were carved from volcanic stone at Rano Raraku, 15 restored moai now stand at Tongariki, and Te Pito Kura is known for one of the largest fallen figures.

The extension includes overnight stays on the island and guided excursions in English-speaking groups. Private services and a Russian-speaking guide are offered for an additional charge. These terms should be distinguished from the [standalone three-day Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), which features private excursions with an English-speaking guide and a different accommodation category. Visiting the same landmarks does not mean identical rates and services.

## Why visit Te Pito Kura?

An ahu is a ceremonial site with a stone platform. Moai were erected on such platforms across the island. Te Pito Kura is known for the O Paro statue, which was transported here from the Rano Raraku area and still lies beside its former installation site. The combination of archaeology and seascape allows you to appreciate the figure and the scale of the work involved.

The enormous moai and local traditions about the site's sacred significance complement each other. Stories of the place's special energy belong to Rapa Nui culture and legend. They are not scientific claims about unusual physical properties of the stones.

## Arranging the optional trip

Easter Island is reached by air from Santiago. Adding this extension changes the total trip length and requires coordination of flights, accommodation, and excursion dates. Visits to archaeological areas within Rapa Nui National Park are arranged with an accredited local guide and a valid admission ticket.

Closed-toe shoes, water, and sun protection are useful. Monuments must be viewed from permitted paths: touching moai, climbing onto platforms, or taking stones and other archaeological objects is prohibited. The rules apply to large groups and private visitors alike.

## Who is this extension for?

If you are already planning [14 days in Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) and want to add Polynesian culture, three days on Rapa Nui will show you a very different side of Chile. If the island and its moai are your main priority, compare the [standalone 3-day tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) without the mainland itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Te Pito Kura included in the compulsory 14-day itinerary?

No. It is listed in a separate 3-day, 2-night Easter Island extension.

### How is Te Pito Kura different from Tongariki?

At [Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), 15 restored moai stand in a row, whereas Te Pito Kura is known for a large fallen statue. These are distinct archaeological sites.

### Do I need a guide?

An accredited local guide is required to visit protected archaeological sites in Rapa Nui National Park.

### Can I choose a tour of Easter Island only?

Yes. The [standalone 3-day program](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) includes Rapa Nui's archaeological monuments without requiring the longer Peru and Bolivia tour.

## Which tours include Ahu Te Pito Kura?

[Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/) is a Rapa Nui archaeological site where the Paro moai lies on the ground. One of the largest statues transported from the quarry and erected on a ceremonial platform, it stood approximately 10 meters tall. A large stone topknot, or pukao, also survives nearby. Here, the focus is a fallen monument rather than a restored row of figures.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include Ahu Te Pito Kura on their main itinerary. The site is typically visited during a full archaeological excursion around [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), along with [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), and [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). It therefore makes sense to begin choosing a tour by comparing how long you spend on the island and the sequence of transfers.

## A three-day itinerary: from the quarry to fallen Paro

[Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) includes Te Pito Kura on the second excursion day. After the south-coast monuments, travelers visit the Rano Raraku quarry, the platform with fifteen moai at Ahu Tongariki, then Te Pito Kura and Anakena Beach. In a single day, you can see where the statues were made, a major restored ensemble, and a monumental figure that remains on the ground.

This is part of a private program, with an English-speaking guide and a packed lunch. A separate excursion devoted solely to Te Pito Kura is not scheduled for that day: the stop forms part of a connected archaeological route.

## A tour with Santiago or a wider journey across Chile

On the [10-day private tour](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/), Te Pito Kura is part of the longer Anakena excursion. Ahu Akahanga, Rano Raraku, and Tongariki come first, followed by the beach and [Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/). The complete program also includes Santiago, Valparaíso, Viña del Mar, and the Maipo Valley.

[Colorful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/) combines Chile's capital with the island's monuments. Its island-day description mentions Tongariki, Te Pito Kura, and Anakena. If the Atacama and Patagonia are also of interest, consider the [12-day Chile itinerary](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/), which combines those regions with Rapa Nui.

## Te Pito Kura on multi-country itineraries

The [17-day grand tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) includes Te Pito Kura on the island's Anakena day alongside Rano Raraku and Tongariki. After Rapa Nui, the journey continues through other regions of Chile, Patagonia, and Argentina.

On the [33-day journey through Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), the platform is visited during an extended tour of the island's archaeological sites. This format brings together several countries and types of experiences; anyone particularly interested in the history of the statues can spend less time on long-distance connections by choosing the three-day island program.

## What Te Pito Kura adds to the excursion

At [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), you can see where sculptures were carved from volcanic tuff. At [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), fifteen moai stand on a restored platform. At Te Pito Kura, Paro lies before you, making it easier to imagine the size of individual statues and the challenges of moving them. [Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/) at Anakena brings the day to a close with another restored complex.

Te Pito Kura is associated with the name 'Navel of the World' and local stories about a special stone. These belong to cultural tradition and excursion narratives, rather than being scientifically verified properties of the site. When selecting a tour, it is more useful to focus on the actual historical monument, the route, and time allowed to explore it.

## Practical considerations

Te Pito Kura is usually visited on the way to the northeastern coast and Anakena. With a packed schedule, check whether enough time remains for stops and a walk by the ocean. On a multi-country journey, also account for flights between Santiago and Easter Island: its distance from the mainland makes the island leg a significant part of the trip.

Protected platforms and sculptures must be viewed from permitted areas. If you are particularly interested in Paro and the history of transporting moai, ask about the guide format and length of the archaeological excursion before choosing a program.

## Frequently asked questions about tours via Te Pito Kura

### What will we see at Ahu Te Pito Kura?

The main attraction is the large fallen Paro moai and the remains of the ceremonial complex. The experience differs from [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) with its restored row of statues.

### Can Te Pito Kura be included in a three-day tour?

Yes. In the [three-day Rapa Nui program](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), the stop is scheduled for day two between Tongariki and Anakena.

### Is Te Pito Kura worth visiting for the 'energy stone'?

The story of the 'Navel of the World' is part of local tradition. The complex's main archaeological value lies in the Paro statue and the history of the island's ceremonial platforms.

## Ahu Tongariki: fifteen moai on Easter Island's coast

Ahu Tongariki is one of the most recognizable archaeological sites on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), which its inhabitants call Rapa Nui. **Fifteen moai** stand on a long stone platform by the ocean, facing inland. A wide coastal landscape stretches behind them; this row of statues often becomes the defining image of a journey to Chilean Polynesia.

UNESCO describes Tongariki as Rapa Nui's most monumental ahu. Yet the site's significance extends beyond the number of statues. It brings together ceremonial platforms, ancestor veneration, the engineering skills of ancient islanders, and modern heritage conservation.

## What is an ahu, and why do the statues stand together?

On Rapa Nui, an **ahu** is a stone ceremonial platform on which moai were erected. Research presented by the Chilean Museum of Pre-Columbian Art links the statues to ancestor worship and the histories of individual lineages. Unlike an isolated sculpture in a museum, an ahu is part of a larger cultural complex, with a forecourt and stone structure.

Tongariki's fifteen moai differ in proportions and features. They are worth viewing from more than just the front: permitted viewpoints reveal differences in silhouettes, heights, and details. The sculptures were carved from volcanic rock; many originated in the [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) area, an ancient quarry on a volcano's slopes.

Standing near the platform, you can ask your guide how these heavy statues were transported to the ocean shore. Archaeologists study various methods of transport and erection; tourist accounts claiming one definitively known method oversimplify a complex subject.

## Why was Tongariki restored?

The present-day line of fifteen upright statues is the result of a major restoration effort. The site's history includes the destruction of monuments and damage associated with the 1960 tsunami. In the late twentieth century, archaeological investigations and reconstruction of the ahu made it possible for visitors to see the complete arrangement once again.

Comparisons with neighboring sites are particularly revealing. Fallen statues lie at [Ahu Vaihu](/chile/place/ahu-vaihu/), while [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/) is known for the separate giant Paro moai, which also remains on the ground. The sites show different states of archaeological heritage. Tongariki lets visitors imagine the ensemble standing upright, while other ahu help explain its history.

Remember that restoration does not grant permission to touch the stones or step onto the platform. Viewing distances are set by national park regulations.

## Sunrise at Ahu Tongariki

Tongariki is especially famous for its sunrises. Morning light rises from the ocean side and the statues form a striking line of silhouettes. The official Chile Travel tourist portal presents an early visit as one way to experience the island and recommends arranging it with a guide in advance.

A sunrise photograph is not guaranteed on every standard moai excursion. For that experience, you need to **plan an early departure from [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/)**, account for sunrise on your chosen date, and observe site-access rules. Your guide must confirm the visit: a standard daytime itinerary and a special sunrise outing are different options.

When taking photographs, keep your distance from the monuments rather than venturing past barriers for a 'better shot.' Agree on an authorized viewpoint with your guide beforehand and allow time to enjoy the site without rushing.

## Tongariki and the Rano Raraku quarry in one day

One of the most rewarding combinations is Ahu Tongariki and [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/). At the quarry, visitors first see moai left on the slopes at various stages of carving and transportation. At Tongariki, they then encounter statues already installed as part of a ceremonial complex.

The sites have different roles and offer different experiences:

| Site | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Rano Raraku | Carving moai from volcanic rock |
| Tongariki | Erecting statues on a ceremonial platform |

A full archaeological day can also include [Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/), [Ahu Vaihu](/chile/place/ahu-vaihu/), and [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/), followed by [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) with its beach and the [Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/) platform. The sequence, however, depends on the time spent at Rano Raraku, the park's operating rules, and the excursion format.

## Tickets, guides, and national park rules

Rapa Nui's archaeological sites belong to a national park added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in **1995**. The park is administered by the local Ma’u Henua community. Under its official rules, visiting requires **an admission ticket and an accredited guide**. This applies even to visitors who arrange their own transport and accommodation.

Tickets can be purchased through the national park website. The administration states that a ticket is valid for **10 consecutive days**; access conditions vary between monuments and should be checked before departure. Special restrictions on the number of entries per ticket apply to Rano Raraku and Orongo.

Touching moai, climbing onto platforms, moving stones, leaving designated paths, and flying drones without authorization are prohibited. Respecting these restrictions is essential to preserving the site, even when it looks open and almost deserted.

## Ada Tours itineraries featuring Ahu Tongariki

In [Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), Tongariki is visited on the second day together with Vaihu, Akahanga, Rano Raraku, Te Pito Kura, and Anakena. On that day, we run a full-day private island excursion with an English-speaking guide and packed lunch. This is a compact route for visitors who want to see the main archaeological monuments without adding numerous mainland cities.

[Colorful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/) combines the island program with Chile's capital and the Pacific coast. Tongariki is visited on a group excursion with an English-speaking guide after Rano Raraku. The itinerary appeals to those who want to contrast Rapa Nui with continental Chile.

On the [10-day Private Tour of Chile and Easter Island](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/), Tongariki likewise follows the quarry, after which the route continues to Te Pito Kura and Anakena. When selecting a tour, compare the time spent on the island itself, the archaeological stops, and the language of guiding.

A reference to Tongariki in the itinerary **does not automatically mean a sunrise visit**. Check this separately against the schedule of the chosen trip.

## Preparing for your visit

Rapa Nui lies in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. Wind, sunshine, and rain can quickly replace one another. For a daytime archaeological excursion, bring comfortable shoes, sun protection, water, and a lightweight windproof and waterproof layer. The main sights lie in open terrain, with usually little shade near the moai.

For a visit lasting several days, grouping sites geographically is more practical: the eastern and southern coasts on one day; the Rano Kau volcano and Orongo ceremonial village on another; and the central monuments and [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) area in a separate segment. This reduces repeated drives across the island and leaves time for your guide's explanations.

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Tongariki

### How many moai stand on the Tongariki platform?

**15 statues.** UNESCO describes this ensemble as the island's most monumental ceremonial ahu.

### Can I see Tongariki at sunrise?

Yes, it is a well-known option. However, you must arrange it with an accredited guide in advance and check access and departure time. A regular daytime excursion does not necessarily include sunrise.

### Are Tongariki and Rano Raraku the same place?

No. [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is the volcanic quarry where moai were made; Tongariki is a separate ceremonial platform with erected statues. It is convenient to visit both in one day.

### Can I enter without a guide?

National park sites require an accredited guide and an admission ticket.

### Which program visits Tongariki along with other monuments?

On the [three-day Rapa Nui tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), it features in a full excursion day with Rano Raraku, Vaihu, Te Pito Kura, and Anakena.

## Optional tours to Ahu Tongariki on Easter Island

[Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is one of Rapa Nui's best-known ceremonial platforms. On Easter Island's eastern coast stand **15 restored stone moai in a row**. They vary in height, proportions, and facial features, with an ocean backdrop behind them.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the option of adding a Tongariki visit. On the [14-day Grand South America Tour: Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/), the principal stops are on the mainland. **Tongariki belongs to an optional 3-day, 2-night Easter Island itinerary.** It is not part of the compulsory visits on the main journey.

## How the optional Rapa Nui program works

Following the main itinerary covering Machu Picchu, Titicaca, Uyuni, and Atacama, travelers may continue to Easter Island. The separate island module features archaeological sites connected with carving and erecting moai: [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), Ahu Tongariki, and [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/). [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) and other island monuments are also included.

It is useful to distinguish two stages in the history of the moai. At the Rano Raraku quarry, the figures were carved from volcanic stone; on ceremonial platforms, they were erected at places important to their communities. At Tongariki, visitors see a restored major complex, quite unlike the fallen statues at Te Pito Kura.

Rapa Nui National Park permits visits to designated archaeological areas when accompanied by an accredited local guide. Tickets, access times, and conduct rules should be arranged before traveling. Visitors may not walk on platforms, touch statues, or leave designated trails.

## When a standalone three-day tour makes more sense

[Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) is a separate travel product. Tongariki features on **day 2**, together with Rano Raraku, Te Pito Kura, and Anakena. Private island excursions with an English-speaking guide are included. The island extension to the grand tour has a different format: excursions in English-speaking groups, with private services and a Russian-speaking guide charged separately.

| Trip format | Tongariki's role |
|---|---|
| [14 days + extension](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) | Separate island program |
| [3 days on Rapa Nui](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) | Main route on day 2 |

This distinction matters: visiting the same landmarks does not mean identical total trip lengths, included services, or payment terms.

## Preparing for the excursion

Flights to Easter Island depart from Santiago, so an additional connection and accommodation are needed. When planning, consider the current Rapa Nui entry rules, confirmation of hotel reservations, and return tickets. Archaeological visits require arrangements with a local guide.

Tongariki stands on an exposed site by the ocean. The sun and wind can feel stronger here than in sheltered city neighborhoods. Closed-toe shoes, water, a hat, and camera protection are recommended. Famous sunrise photographs of the moai do not guarantee that **a standard daytime excursion arrives at sunrise**; check the visiting time on the specific itinerary.

For more options, explore [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and the [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/) theme. The [Tongariki destination page](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) explains the monument and its archaeological importance.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many moai are on the Tongariki platform?

Fifteen stone statues stand on the restored platform.

### Is the visit included in the main 14-day tour?

No. Tongariki belongs to the three-day Easter Island extension. The main program covers mainland Peru, Bolivia, and Chile.

### Can Tongariki be visited without the longer South America tour?

Yes. It is included on day 2 of the [standalone three-day Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/).

### How is Tongariki different from Rano Raraku?

[Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is the quarry where moai were carved; Tongariki is a ceremonial platform with a restored row of statues.

## Which tours let you see the fifteen moai of Ahu Tongariki?

[Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) stands near the [Rano Raraku volcanic quarry](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) on Easter Island. Fifteen restored statues form a long row against the open coastline. The platform suffered damage as ancient structures were destroyed and later from the 1960 tsunami; the complex was restored in the 1990s. Today, visitors can appreciate the layout of the ceremonial ensemble, the statues' scale, and the archaeologists' work.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose main itineraries include Tongariki. The monument is one of the central stops on a Rapa Nui sightseeing day. When choosing, consider not only whether it is on the route, but how much time remains for Rano Raraku, other ahu, and relaxation on the island.

## Three days on Rapa Nui: a compact Tongariki program

[Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) schedules Tongariki on the second day. The route covers south-coast monuments, Rano Raraku, Tongariki, [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/), and [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). After a walk by the ocean, travelers return to the hotel. It is a busy day, but you get to see several kinds of archaeological sites on a single excursion.

Day three includes [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), [Ahu Hanga Poukura](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/), [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), and [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/). This makes it possible to group visits by subject: moai production and major coastal platforms on one day, the island's central sites on another.

## When to choose a trip via Santiago

The [10-day Private Tour of Chile and Easter Island](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/) adds Santiago, Valparaíso, Viña del Mar, and the Maipo Valley to the island excursions. On Rapa Nui, Tongariki appears on the Anakena excursion with Rano Raraku, Te Pito Kura, and the [Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/) platform by the beach. Other days are reserved for additional archaeological sites.

[Colorful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/) includes a full-day group excursion with an English-speaking guide. The [12-day Best of Chile journey](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/) combines Tongariki with the Atacama Desert, Torres del Paine, and other island monuments. With this choice, extra time is spent flying between regions: it is a journey across Chile as a whole, not just Rapa Nui.

## Longer itineraries through South America

On the [17-day Chile and Argentina itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), Tongariki is included in a full day of island archaeology. The journey then continues through Atacama, Patagonia, and other South American regions. The [33-day tour through Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) also features Tongariki, but the visit follows an extended journey through other countries.

Both options suit travelers wishing to discover several cultural and natural regions. If the moai and Rapa Nui itself are your main interest, the [three-day island itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) is geographically simpler and avoids additional mainland legs.

## Rano Raraku and Tongariki: why visit both?

[Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is known for the quarry where most moai were carved. Statues can be seen here at different stages of production. Tongariki shows the outcome: figures erected on a ceremonial platform. A stop at [Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/) with its enormous fallen Paro moai adds a third perspective to the history of the sculptures.

For travelers interested in Rapa Nui culture, this sequence is richer in meaning than choosing just one photogenic site. Programs listing all of these places allow you to compare their roles in island society.

## Visiting times and sunrise at Ahu Tongariki

Tongariki is often pictured at sunrise. The platform is indeed famous for the early sun appearing behind the moai, but **a sunrise visit does not automatically follow from the monument appearing on an itinerary**. In the tours listed, Tongariki usually forms part of a full-day excursion around the island. If sunrise is important, arrange the timing and possibility of a separate early departure in advance.

When planning, account for the flight via Santiago, the number of nights on the island, and the order of excursions. Weather, wind, and national park rules may affect the outing. Statues and platforms must be viewed from the permitted distance, without walking onto the ancient structures.

## Frequently asked questions about tours via Ahu Tongariki

### How many moai stand at Ahu Tongariki?

Fifteen moai stand on the restored platform. It is one of the largest archaeological ensembles on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/).

### Can Tongariki and Rano Raraku be visited in one day?

Yes. On the [three-day island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), both are included in the day-two excursion with Te Pito Kura and Anakena.

### Is a Tongariki sunrise included in every tour?

No. A standard monument excursion does not imply an early sunrise departure. If this matters to you, check for a separate visit on the particular itinerary.

### How is Tongariki different from Ahu Akivi?

[Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is a coastal platform with fifteen statues; [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) has seven moai in the island's interior. They are usually separate stops on different excursion days.
